<!--
The Graduate School sets the line spacing of a dissertation part by part. The
body is double spaced; a block quotation is single spaced and indented half an
inch from both margins; the entries of the reference list are single spaced
within an entry and double spaced between one entry and the next.
-->

# An Introduction Whose Title Is Long Enough to Turn Over Onto a Second Line of the Table of Contents

The body is double spaced, and runs on for long enough here that its line
spacing can be measured against the quotation and the references below it
without any guessing about which line belongs to what.

> A block quotation is single spaced and indented half an inch from the left
> margin and half an inch from the right, which is narrower than the body and
> is what marks it out as quoted rather than written.

Some text after the quotation [@schneiderCattellHornCarrollTheoryCognitive2018;
@austenMansfieldPark1990], so that the list below has two entries and the
space between them can be measured as well as the space inside them.

A sentence carrying a note.^[A note is a numbered entry, single spaced
within itself and long enough here to run onto a second line so that its
spacing can be measured.] And a second one.^[The note after it, so that the
space between two notes can be measured as well.]
